title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
lines: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence connects learning, reasoning, language, perception, and planning.
Its eleven chapters compare methods rather than present intelligence as one mysterious ingredient.
Readers gain a map for asking what a system does and how it does it.

title: Rules or examples?
lines: Imagine identifying a pattern from examples, then checking an explicit rule.
Learning and symbolic reasoning approach these tasks differently.
The book explains their strengths and limitations before considering combinations.

title: A goal needs a plan
lines: Recognizing something is different from choosing actions under constraints.
The planning chapters connect goals, search, and adaptation when conditions change.
The ethics discussion then asks who is affected and who remains accountable.
